newsitem.title: GERMANY: Institute calls on Bonn to abandon savings package.
newsitem.headline: Institute calls on Bonn to abandon savings package.

text.p: A leading German economic institute on Wednesday called on Bonn to abandon its planned austerity programme, saying it would choke off demand and damage the economy.

"Spending cuts at the wrong time will weaken rather than strengthen economic development and so be counterproductive," the DIW, a left-leaning institute which often supports the opposition Social Democrats, said in its latest report.
It said because of weak demand the government should let its deficit rise in order not to weaken the economy.
Bonn is hoping to do exactly the opposite.

It plans to slash public spending by 50 billion marks and social security spending by 20 billion next year to ensure the public deficit gets back under the three percent of gross domestic product level targetted for countries wishing to qualify for the single European currency.
But the government is also depending on robust economic growth to lower its deficit from around 3.5 percent of GDP.
The DIW said the government should halve the solidarity surcharge on income tax immediately, rather than reduce it gradually. This would give a badly needed boost to demand, it said.
The DIW added that Germany's public deficit should be cut eventually but said now was not the right time.

It estimated that the total public deficit would grow to 130 billion marks this year from 111 billion in 1995 because of falling tax revenues and higher spending on unemployment caused by the economic slowdown around the turn of the year.
It also predicted that the federal deficit would be 76 billion marks instead of the planned 60 billion marks.
